title: Think in vectors
outcome: Implement batched predictions with NumPy and build a player similarity explorer.

blocks.body: Question: Can a whole season be one calculation?
Mathematics: Learn vectors, matrix shapes, dot products, norms, projections, rank, and feature scaling.

Dataset: StatsBomb Open Data: competitions.json → matches/{competition_id}/{season_id}.json. Use scores, dates, and information available before kickoff. Build recent-form features only from earlier matches. Player similarity uses player statistics aggregated from event files; restrict these to training matches.
Reading: Mathematics for Machine Learning chapters 2 and 3. Read only the sections used by the experiments.

blocks.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
blocks.note: Use selected sections as a reference after the visual experiment. The authors provide a free PDF.

blocks.title: 3Blue1Brown · visual mathematics
blocks.note: Find the linear algebra and calculus lessons. Recreate one visual idea in code.

blocks.body: Challenge: Calculate a small dot product yourself. Diagnose a shape error and explain one misleading similarity result.

tasks.prompt: Represent matches as rows and pre-match measurements as columns. Annotate every matrix shape.
